interest: Shows SCAP-Washington conflict over 1949 yen devaluation, and wartime scrip and Brazilian claims entangling Japan's finances.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.515) covers financial, monetary, and currency questions concerning Japan between July and December 1949 during the Allied Occupation. The documents encompass four primary matters: consular and Treasury investigations into the validity of Japanese wartime military dollar notes held in the Netherlands; the intense debate between SCAP (General MacArthur) and Washington interagency officials (State, Treasury, Federal Reserve, and economic adviser Joseph Dodge) regarding whether to devalue the Japanese yen following the 1949 sterling devaluation; diplomatic efforts by the Japanese Foreign Office and U.S. officials regarding frozen Japanese diplomatic funds in Brazil needed by Sweden to continue serving as protecting power for Japanese interests; and the legal and budgetary elimination of 152 million Type B military yen held by the Bank of Japan through accounting transfers into the Japanese 'termination of war' budget to extinguish potential claims against the United States.

subfiles.about: Transmitting two Japanese-issued dollar currency notes received from a Dutch bank to Washington for examination and valuation.
subfiles.from: Edward C. Wilkinson, Commercial Attaché, American Embassy, The Hague
subfiles.summary: Dutch bank asks about the value of old Japanese wartime dollar notes; Wilkinson forwards them to Treasury.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 282 from American Embassy The Hague regarding Japanese dollar currency inquiry

subfiles.about: Advising that the Japanese dollar notes examined by the Treasury Department were issued for military purposes and hold only souvenir value.
subfiles.from: Mr. Stuart, Office of International Finance, Treasury Department
subfiles.summary: Treasury's Stuart confirms the Japanese wartime notes have no value beyond being souvenirs.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Memorandum from Stuart to Knapp on Japanese dollar currency

subfiles.about: Returning the Japanese dollar notes to The Hague and reporting the Treasury Department's finding that they are valueless military currency.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State (drafted by E. Doherty, OFD)
keywords: Office of Financial and Development Policy
subfiles.summary: State tells The Hague the Japanese wartime notes have no value beyond being souvenirs, returning them.
subfiles.title: State Department Despatch to American Mission The Hague on Japanese dollar currency
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, The Hague

subfiles.about: Reporting on the partial shipment of three million U.S. dollars aboard the SS Reinholt from Tientsin.
subfiles.from: Walter P. McConaughy, American Consul General, Shanghai
subfiles.summary: McConaughy reports only $1 million of a $3 million Tientsin dollar shipment loaded for transport from Shanghai.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 4130 from Shanghai on shipment of U.S. dollars from Tientsin

subfiles.about: Analyzing interagency disagreements between SCAP and Washington over the proposed devaluation of the Japanese yen.
subfiles.from: Noel Hemmendinger, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs
subfiles.summary: Hemmendinger: SCAP opposes devaluing the yen, but State, Treasury, and the Fed favor roughly 15%, referring the dispute to the National Advisory Council and adviser Dodge.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum from Hemmendinger to Allison on yen devaluation
subfiles.to: John M. Allison, Director, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs

subfiles.about: Reporting on Brazilian restrictions on Japanese diplomatic funds used by Sweden to protect Japanese interests.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan (Ware Adams), Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Adams reports Brazil barred withdrawals from Japan's blocked account, straining Swedish protection of Japanese interests; Matsui sought US help, but Adams said the US can't intervene.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 812 from Tokyo on protection of Japanese interests in Brazil

subfiles.about: Detailing the depletion of Japanese diplomatic funds in Brazil and Sweden's inability to fund representation activities.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Foreign Office memo: Sweden, short of funds, warns it may end its protection of Japanese nationals in Brazil, Chile, and Peru after Brazil blocked most of the account.
subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Office Memorandum on expenses of Swedish Legation in Brazil
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Recommending an accounting settlement for 152 million Type B military yen held by the Japanese Ministry of Finance to preempt claims against the U.S.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports Japan holds 152 million unredeemed Type B military yen, risking a claim against the US.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 546 from Tokyo on Type B military yen holdings

subfiles.about: Confirming the liquidation of potential U.S. liability for Type B military yen by charging it to Japan's termination of war budget.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Sebald confirms the 152 million yen was absorbed into Japan's war-termination budget, ending any claim basis.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 593 from Tokyo on settlement of Type B military yen
